verdict.rationale: ByteAsk's own docs say it compiles, runs your test suite and sanitizers, and drives gdb. It then presents a diff for review before making permanent changes, and the headless exec mode lets those checks run in CI pipelines. That covers both parts of the story: inspecting diffs and running checks before changes land. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration (all evidence is vendor docs), and explicit documentation of pull-request or merge-gate integration beyond reviewing diffs before permanent changes.

support.subject: As a developer, I can inspect diffs and run checks to catch problems before merging

citations.quote: edits files, compiles, runs tests, and presents a diff for your review before making permanent changes
drives the real toolchain - sanitizers, your test suite, and any gdb session you already have open - and hands you a diff that survived the debugger
A read-only run can still build your program under AddressSanitizer and run it.
For scripting and CI pipelines, use the `exec` subcommand
